description:
List the projects this R3 account can work on — its own and its teams' — last updated first, with the projectId every other project tool takes. It is how a project the user names ("my slot machine") rather than giving an id is found: search for it; its projectId is what r3_project_load takes.

Search by name rather than paging: search: "slot" is matched (case-insensitively, anywhere in the name) against EVERY project by the server, not against the page you are holding. Names are not unique: when more than one project matches, the candidates' name, team and last save tell them apart, and which one is meant is the user's answer.

Each row says whose space it is in (personal, or a team by name), the account's role on it (a viewer cannot save changes), whether it is in the R3 Community, and whether you (this agent key or app connection) created it.

cursor.description: Continue a previous listing: pass the nextCursor it returned, unchanged. Omit for the first page.

search.description: Match this text against project names, on the server (case-insensitive). Omit for every project.

name: r3_project_list

answer.description: This answer in words: what was done, what R3 measured, decided or refused, and what to do next. The same text as the result's text block. Read it: the fields beside it are the data, this is the guidance.

title: List the R3 projects this account can work on
